check.reason: Melian shares none of this text, which the reviewing host's store and terminal hold

message.text: `melianInstall()` reads Melian's install with the default `past: "fails"`, limited to `maxInstallDirectories` (50,000). The limit is sized for Melian's own install; the decision calls it "22 times this repository's install". But `Install.read` takes the install root as the outermost ancestor that holds a `node_modules`, and it walks every tree there. So the count covers whatever else shares that root. In a global install (`npm install -g`, root `/usr/local/lib`) that means every other global package. Under a stray `~/node_modules` above a clone, it means everything in that home directory. Once that count passes 50,000, `#scan` throws `InstalledPackagesError`. Every producer calls `melianInstall()`: `runIdentity` in checks.ts, `lensRequest`, `adjudicationInput`, `recordDismissal` and `startAdjudication`. So every review and every dismissal aborts.

evidence.snippet:
// The most directories Melian reads to key an install; past it, keying fails or the install is unidentified.
export const maxInstallDirectories = 50_000;

**A bound.** The walk reads at most `maxInstallDirectories`, 50,000 directories, and past it fails the key: "Melian cannot key its install: it holds more than 50000 directories." That is 22 times this repository's install. A global install whose root is `/usr/lib` reads every global package, and one that big fails closed rather than walk without end.

A module whose path cannot be read, a module beneath no `node_modules`, and an install past the bound each fail the key with a reason, and a review that keys Melian's install, or the instrumenter's for `list_mutants`, fails with it. The key never holds an empty or partial list. Those three stay failures: none is a layout a review can work around, and a review that ran under them would key nothing. On 2026-11-21 the coordinator corrected the bound for the instrumenter's install, after Melian's round at `5cc5b261f` found that a customer monorepo of more than 50,000 directories, an ordinary layout the base reviewed, aborted every review that offered `list_mutants`: the bound was sized for Melian's own install. Past it, the walk of the instrumenter's install stops, reading no further directory and following no further link, and leaves the install unidentified with its root, `.`, in `unrecognised`, so the review runs and reuses nothing; Melian's own install still fails at the bound.

explanation.what: `melianInstall()` reads Melian's install with the default `past: "fails"`, limited to `maxInstallDirectories` (50,000). The limit is sized for Melian's own install; the decision calls it "22 times this repository's install". But `Install.read` takes the install root as the outermost ancestor that holds a `node_modules`, and it walks every tree there. So the count covers whatever else shares that root. In a global install (`npm install -g`, root `/usr/local/lib`) that means every other global package. Under a stray `~/node_modules` above a clone, it means everything in that home directory. Once that count passes 50,000, `#scan` throws `InstalledPackagesError`. Every producer calls `melianInstall()`: `runIdentity` in checks.ts, `lensRequest`, `adjudicationInput`, `recordDismissal` and `startAdjudication`. So every review and every dismissal aborts.
explanation.whatToDo: Count the bound against what Melian's code can reach, not the whole outermost root. Or read Melian's own install with `past: "unidentified"`, as `TypeScriptMutationAdapter.install()` does, so a large shared root costs reuse and not the review. Keep the hard failure only for the cases that cannot produce a key at all: a module that cannot be read, or one beneath no node_modules.
explanation.whyHere: The limit exists to cap the cost of keying Melian's install. Instead it counts packages that are not Melian's, and it turns them into a hard failure. The base keyed `piVersions` through `installedVersion` and never walked a tree, so it reviewed on any global prefix. This change already found the same flaw for the instrumenter's install (Melian's round at 5cc5b261f) and fixed that case with `"unidentified"`. It left Melian's own read on `"fails"`, even though Melian's own read reaches the same kind of large root.

properties.failureScenario: A user installs the published CLI globally with `npm install -g @melian-agent/cli`, beside other large global tools such as firebase-tools, @aws-amplify/cli, @angular/cli and npm itself, under `/usr/local/lib/node_modules`. pipeline's `dist/code-version.js` lives at `/usr/local/lib/node_modules/@melian-agent/cli/node_modules/@melian-agent/pipeline/dist/`. Of its ancestors, `/usr/local/lib` holds a `node_modules`, so `Install.read` sets the root there (installed-packages.ts:52-53) and queues `/usr/local/lib/node_modules`, which holds every global package. Once those trees pass 50,000 directories, `#scan` (installed-packages.ts:206-210) throws "Melian cannot key its install: it holds more than 50000 directories." `melian review` then fails before any check runs, because `runIdentity` calls `melianInstall()`. `melian dismiss` fails the same way, and `melian doctor` reports a `packages` failure with exit 1. At base, that same install reviewed normally. A second route to the same failure: a maintainer's clone sits under a home directory that holds a stray `~/node_modules` from an accidental `npm install`. That directory becomes the root, is walked in full and counts against the bound.
